title: pending_pause_overflow cleared on panic-unwind silently drops queued ERROR
evidence: On panic during a pause/resume cycle, the pending_pause_overflow queue is cleared without flushing — silent drop instead of structured ERROR synthesis.
recommendation: Drain the queue into ERROR cascades before clearing, or guard with RAII so the unwind path delivers the diagnostic.

title: Core::up(INVALIDATE) cascades via dep-walk instead of plain-forward
evidence: R1.4.2 specifies plain-forward semantics for INVALIDATE; current impl runs the cascade through dep-walk in Core::invalidate. Behavioral effect is identical for canonical scenarios but the implementation diverges from spec. RESOLVED 2026-05-22 by D281 (commit 602cd1b, 'fix(D281): Core::up(Invalidate) R1.4.2 plain-forward Commit 3 of 3'). node.rs:2627–2647 now implements plain-forward; TS arm was already R1.4.2-conformant, Rust convergence completes the cross-impl alignment. Decision: ~/src/graphrefly-ts/docs/rust-port-decisions.md D281.
recommendation: Either lift the impl to plain-forward, or amend canonical-spec to bless dep-walk semantics. Track until alignment is decided.

title: Phase 3 of Core::register walks deps twice
evidence: Validation walks deps once in Phase 1 (lock-released) and again in Phase 3 (re-validation under state-lock). Caching the validated NodeId vector between phases removes one O(N) walk and a HashMap::get per dep.
recommendation: Cache validated NodeIds in a phase-1 scratch buffer; re-use in phase 3.

title: reset_for_fresh_lifecycle calls make_op_scratch lock-held
evidence: Lock-discipline asymmetry: make_op_scratch is lock-released in Core::register but lock-held inside reset_for_fresh_lifecycle. Inconsistent lock discipline across the same helper. RESOLVED 2026-05-22 (STRUCTURALLY HARDENED via rustdoc contract upgrade — verified at migration-status.md:299). node.rs:641–643 now documents that the lock-held make_op_scratch call is safe because binding.retain_handle is a leaf operation per op_state.rs:69–80; this is not an inconsistency to lift but an established safety contract. The asymmetry was a doc gap, not a lock-discipline bug.
recommendation: Lift make_op_scratch out of the lock-held region in reset_for_fresh_lifecycle to match Core::register.

title: Asymmetric UnknownNode typed-error surface across Graph wrapper
evidence: Graph::derived returns Result<NodeId, NameError> for namespace conflicts; underlying Core call returns RegisterError. The wrapper layer doesn't surface RegisterError::UnknownDep distinctly. Callers can't differentiate name-conflict vs unknown-dep.
recommendation: Unify the wrapper error surface so RegisterError variants flow through with their semantic identity preserved.

title: Schedule Slice E2 — fn ctx + cleanup hooks
evidence: D054/D055 design locked 2026-05-07 for ctx + cleanup hooks per R2.4.5/R2.4.6. Implementation deferred. Open design questions: (a) ctx extends/replaces FnCtx, (b) binding-side storage shape. RESOLVED — Slice E2 landed; R2.4.5/R2.4.6 cleanup hooks are first-class on FnCtx. Evidence: node.rs:504 'OnDeactivation cleanup hook BEFORE producer_deactivate'; node.rs:3162 'wipe_ctx cleanup hook fires'; node.rs:3388 'Slice E2 (R2.4.6 / D055): on resubscribable terminal reset, fire ...'; node.rs:4467 'Per R1.3.9.c never-populated case, OnInvalidate cleanup hook'. D054/D055 decisions both shipped.
recommendation: Lift Slice E2 once the two design questions resolve.

title: Schedule TS port-back of PausableMode consolidation
evidence: Rust port adopted PausableMode { Default, ResumeAll, Off } as the canonical §2.6 model. TS still ships ResumeAll as default. Port-back scheduled in Phase 13.6.B migration scope.
recommendation: Land PausableMode rename + Default-as-canonical change in TS; keep behavior gated on opt-in flag during migration.

title: node.rs is 5.5K LOC — architectural splitting candidate
evidence: node.rs is now 5459 LOC as of 2026-05-24 (was 4.6K at original audit 2026-05-09; +20% growth post-Slice F+G+H+E2+M4+M5+M5.B+S-sequence+D266–D287 work). Concentration of dispatcher + lifecycle + register + pause logic still highest in the workspace; D272–D274 vestigial cleanup pass recovered some surface but did not split. batch.rs is the #2 hotspot at 4044 LOC. Cognitive load scales non-linearly past ~3K LOC; current state exceeds that threshold by ~80%.
recommendation: Investigate splitting along orthogonal concerns: dispatcher.rs (Core::up/emit/resolve), register.rs (Core::register), pause.rs (Core::pause/resume), terminal.rs (Core::complete/cleanup). Quantify with cargo-modules + per-fn LOC.

title: Only 18 of 266 spec rules have a doc-comment citation
evidence: Re-extracted 2026-05-24: items.jsonl shows 18 distinct rule IDs cited across all crate doc comments. The canonical spec now defines 266 rule IDs (grew from 222 at original audit). Gap widened to 93% (was 89%). Test-side coverage healthier: 68 tests cite ≥1 rule; 32 distinct rules have ≥1 test citation. The doc-comment-citation gap continued to widen as M4/M5/Slice U–W/native-ship/D266–D287 work landed without per-rule breadcrumbs on the substrate side.
recommendation: Decide whether to (a) require rule-comment density at PR review time or (b) accept that high-traffic rules carry citations and the rest live in tests. Either way, surface the gap so it's a deliberate choice.
